context.analysis:
## Overview
The system is an Amazon-style global online bookstore handling physical and electronic books with integrated recommendations, reviews, and secure checkout. It is architected for high availability, strict regulatory compliance, and sub-2-second performance across multiple regions.

## Key Elements
- **Users**: Guest Buyer, Registered Buyer, Store Administrator, and Third-Party Vendor/Publisher.
- **Software System**: Online Bookstore (Global e-commerce platform).
- **External Systems**: Stripe/PayPal (Payment Gateway), FedEx/UPS (Shipping Provider API), AWS SES (Email/Notification Service), and AWS Cognito/Auth0 (Identity Provider).
- **Infrastructure**: AWS Cloud across us-east-1, eu-west-1, and ap-southeast-1.

## Relationships
- Customers and Vendors interact with the Online Bookstore via HTTPS/TLS 1.3 (Web/Mobile).
- Users authenticate via Identity Provider using OIDC/OAuth2 over HTTPS/JWT.
- Online Bookstore integrates with Payment Gateway and Shipping Provider API via outbound HTTPS/REST with circuit breakers.
- Edge routing managed globally via AWS Route 53 latency-based routing.

## Technology Stack
- **Cloud & Edge**: AWS (us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1) with Route 53 for multi-region active-active traffic distribution.
- **Security & Identity**: AWS Cognito or Auth0 for federated OIDC/OAuth2 authentication, AWS WAF for perimeter defense against OWASP Top-10.
- **Networking & Transport**: TLS 1.3 for all ingress/egress, mTLS (AWS App Mesh/Istio) for container communication.
- **Data & Secrets**: Regionally isolated databases with AES-256 storage encryption and AWS Secrets Manager for dynamic secret injection.
- **Observability**: AWS X-Ray and OpenTelemetry for distributed tracing and logging.

## Rationale
This multi-region active-active AWS architecture ensures 99.95% availability and sub-2-second performance on 3G networks by minimizing cross-border latency and isolating traffic regionally. Strict data residency boundaries and managed identity federation guarantee GDPR and CCPA compliance while protecting sensitive customer PII.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
- E-commerce online bookstore for buying physical and electronic books with recommendations and reviews.
- Deployed on AWS across us-east-1, eu-west-1, and ap-southeast-1 to handle 1M MAU with 99.95% uptime.

## Key Elements
- Single Page Application (React.js, AWS S3, CloudFront)
- API Gateway (AWS API Gateway, AWS Cognito JWT validation)
- Core E-Commerce Container (Node.js/TypeScript)
- Recommendation & Review Container (Python, FastAPI)
- Tax & Currency Container (Node.js)
- Databases (Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon ElastiCache Redis)
- Event Bus & Integration (Amazon SQS/SNS, third-party shipping and tax/currency APIs)

## Relationships
- SPA to API Gateway: HTTPS / WSS
- API Gateway to Fargate Containers: Internal VPC Application Load Balancers (gRPC / HTTPS)
- Services to Databases: PostgreSQL wire protocol, DynamoDB API, Redis protocol
- Asynchronous Events: Amazon SQS / SNS

## Technology Stack
- React.js / S3 / CloudFront: High-performance frontend delivery for <2s page load times
- AWS API Gateway & Cognito: Scalable entry point with secure JWT validation
- Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate: Consistent container orchestration across multiple regions
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL & DynamoDB: Transactional and low-latency storage with global replication and geo-fencing
- Amazon ElastiCache Redis: Local caching for recommendations to protect performance

## Rationale
- Multi-region Fargate deployment ensures 99.95% availability and scalability for 1M MAU while meeting strict GDPR/CCPA data residency rules.
- Isolated microservices support specialized domains like recommendations and multi-currency taxation without compromising page performance.

Single Page Application.analysis:
## Overview
- Single Page Application (SPA) container for the Online Bookstore e-commerce platform.
- Delivers a high-performance, secure, and accessible user interface for global customers and administrators.

## Key Elements
- Router Component (`React Router v6`)
- State Management Store (`Zustand`)
- API Client Layer (`Axios`)
- Feature Modules (Catalog Browser, Checkout Flow, Review Manager, Recommendation Widget)
- External Infrastructure (AWS S3, AWS CloudFront, AWS API Gateway)

## Relationships
- Router Component loads Feature Modules on-demand [In-Memory]
- Feature Modules and State Management Store read/write state [In-Memory]
- Feature Modules and State Management Store invoke API Client Layer [TypeScript / HTTPS]
- API Client Layer sends requests to AWS API Gateway [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- React.js: Frontend UI library chosen for component reusability and fast rendering.
- React Router v6: Handles client-side navigation with code-splitting for <2s page load times on 3G.
- Zustand: Lightweight state management ensuring tokens are kept strictly in-memory for security.
- Axios: HTTP client with interceptors for JWT injection and multi-currency headers.
- AWS S3 & CloudFront: Static asset storage and global edge distribution for high availability.

## Rationale
- This architecture guarantees sub-2-second page loads and 99.95% uptime globally across target AWS regions.
- Strict in-memory state handling and CSP headers ensure robust GDPR/CCPA compliance and OWASP Top-10 mitigations.

API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The Online Bookstore API Gateway is a globally distributed entry point designed to secure, route, and optimize traffic for an e-commerce platform. It provides scalable request handling, authentication, and traffic management across multiple AWS regions while ensuring GDPR and CCPA compliance.

## Key Elements
- **Request Router / Reverse Proxy (AWS API Gateway / Envoy Proxy):** Terminates TLS, enforces rate limits, handles CORS, and inspects locale headers for multi-currency routing.
- **Authentication & Authorization Filter Component:** Validates JWT tokens against AWS Cognito/Auth0 and executes user-ID-based rate limiting and RBAC.
- **Request/Response Transformation Component:** Performs schema validation, payload sanitization, and dynamic PII masking for GDPR compliance.
- **Circuit Breaker & Traffic Management Component:** Implements adaptive traffic shedding to prioritize checkout traffic during high-load events.
- **Telemetry & Analytics Interceptor:** Asynchronously scrubs and streams anonymized usage metrics to the event bus.

## Relationships
- **SPA & Vendors -> Request Router:** Incoming client and vendor traffic [HTTPS / WSS via Amazon CloudFront with AWS WAF]
- **Request Router -> Auth Filter:** Validates incoming authentication tokens [Internal In-Memory / gRPC]
- **Circuit Breaker -> Core / Rec / Tax Containers:** Forwards prioritized requests [gRPC over internal Application Load Balancers with mTLS]
- **Telemetry Interceptor -> Amazon SQS/SNS:** Publishes decoupled usage and analytics metrics [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- **AWS API Gateway / Envoy Proxy:** Chosen for low-latency global routing, rate limiting, and edge security integrations.
- **AWS WAF & CloudFront:** Deployed for DDoS protection, OWASP Top-10 mitigation, and multi-region content delivery.
- **AWS Cognito / Auth0:** Utilized for OIDC/OAuth2 identity management and secure JWT token validation.
- **Terraform / AWS CDK:** Used for GitOps-driven infrastructure deployment and consistent multi-region configuration across `us-east-1`, `eu-west-1`, and `ap-southeast-1`.

## Rationale
This architecture ensures 99.95% uptime and high availability through multi-region deployment, circuit breaking, and rapid failover mechanisms. Strict mTLS, PII masking, and AWS WAF controls fulfill rigorous security, GDPR, and CCPA requirements while protecting core checkout revenue.

Core E-Commerce Container.analysis:
## Overview
Modular monolithic architecture for the Core E-Commerce Container built with Node.js and TypeScript on Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate. It manages catalogue browsing, secure shopping carts, order fulfillment, and notifications while adhering to high-availability and compliance standards.

## Key Elements
- **Catalogue Component**: NestJS module managing product browsing and search via TypeORM.
- **Cart & Checkout Component**: NestJS module handling ephemeral cart states and tokenized payment processing.
- **Order Fulfillment Component**: Manages order state transitions and third-party logistics integration.
- **Customer Notification Component**: Handles transactional communications via AWS SES.
- **Data Stores**: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, Amazon DynamoDB, and Amazon ElastiCache Redis.

## Relationships
- API Gateway -> Core E-Commerce Container via gRPC / HTTPS
- Core E-Commerce Container -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL via PostgreSQL wire protocol
- Core E-Commerce Container -> Amazon DynamoDB via DynamoDB API
- Core E-Commerce Container -> Amazon ElastiCache Redis for cart state management
- Core E-Commerce Container -> Stripe/PayPal via Outbound HTTPS/REST
- Core E-Commerce Container -> FedEx/UPS via Outbound HTTPS/REST
- Core E-Commerce Container -> AWS SES via Outbound HTTPS/API
- Core E-Commerce Container -> Amazon SQS/SNS via asynchronous event publishing

## Technology Stack
- **Node.js / TypeScript**: Core runtime language providing rapid feature delivery and unified backend tooling.
- **NestJS**: Modular framework enforcing strict directory-level boundaries and dependency injection.
- **Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate**: Serverless container orchestration for scalable, isolated execution.
- **Amazon ElastiCache Redis**: Low-latency, ephemeral storage for cart session management and seamless user login merges.
- **AWS Secrets Manager**: Secure runtime injection and rotation of database credentials and API keys.

## Rationale
Modular NestJS design within a single Fargate runtime minimizes initial operational complexity while maintaining strict internal boundaries for future microservice extraction. Integrated resilience patterns, tokenized payments, and OpenTelemetry instrumentation satisfy strict performance, multi-currency, and compliance requirements.

Recommendation & Review Container.analysis:
## Overview
The Recommendation & Review Container provides secure book recommendations and user reviews for the Online Bookstore. It runs on Python and FastAPI within AWS ECS Fargate, ensuring scalability and 99.95% uptime.

## Key Elements
- **Review API Component**: FastAPI application handling review CRUD operations, moderation flags, and verified purchase badging.
- **Recommendation Query Component**: FastAPI application serving low-latency "Customers also bought" suggestions.
- **Recommendation Worker Component**: Decoupled Python background worker processing purchase events.
- **Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL**: Relational database for persistent storage of reviews and purchase histories.
- **Amazon ElastiCache Redis**: In-memory cache for fast recommendation lookups with Multi-AZ replication.
- **Amazon SQS / SNS**: Event bus used for triggering background workers and publishing analytics.

## Relationships
- **API Gateway -> Review API / Recommendation Query**: Routes HTTP/REST requests [HTTPS]
- **Review API / Recommendation Query -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL**: Reads and writes transactional data [TCP / PostgreSQL Wire Protocol with TLS]
- **Recommendation Query -> Amazon ElastiCache Redis**: Fetches cached recommendations [Redis TCP with TLS and AUTH]
- **Amazon SQS -> Recommendation Worker**: Triggers asynchronous background model updates [AWS SDK / SQS API]
- **Recommendation Query -> Event Bus (SNS)**: Logs impression and click-through metrics [AWS SDK]

## Technology Stack
- **Python with FastAPI**: High-performance asynchronous framework chosen for rapid API development and Pydantic validation.
- **Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate**: Serverless container orchestration to maintain scalability and simplify infrastructure management.
- **Amazon ElastiCache Redis**: Distributed caching layer to achieve sub-second page loads and recommendation delivery.
- **Pydantic**: Data validation library used to sanitize inputs and prevent XSS or SQL injection.
- **AWS Secrets Manager**: Secure storage for database credentials and Redis auth tokens.

## Rationale
Decoupling the recommendation worker via SQS isolates heavy data processing from public APIs to meet scalability requirements for 1M MAU. Multi-AZ Redis caching with graceful database fallbacks ensures high availability, strict security compliance, and sub-second performance.

Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL.analysis:
## Overview
The Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database system serves as the core transactional data store for the Online Bookstore. It ensures secure, highly available, and compliant multi-region storage for e-commerce transactions, customer data, and catalogs.

## Key Elements
* **Writer Instance**: Primary Aurora PostgreSQL engine handling regional write traffic.
* **Reader Instances**: Aurora PostgreSQL read replicas scaled horizontally across availability zones.
* **Cluster Endpoint (Writer)**: DNS routing component directing write traffic.
* **Reader Endpoint**: Load-balanced DNS endpoint for read queries.
* **Amazon RDS Proxy**: Connection pooler securing and managing database connections.
* **Aurora Distributed Storage**: Asynchronously replicated global storage layer across AWS regions (`us-east-1`, `eu-west-1`, `ap-southeast-1`).

## Relationships
* Core E-Commerce Container -> **Cluster Endpoint (Writer)**: Transmits transactional writes [PostgreSQL wire protocol / TLS 1.3].
* Core E-Commerce Container -> **Reader Endpoint**: Transmits read queries [PostgreSQL wire protocol / TLS 1.3].
* **Reader Endpoint** -> **Amazon RDS Proxy**: Pools and forwards read traffic [PostgreSQL wire protocol].
* **Amazon RDS Proxy** -> **Reader Instances**: Manages query distribution [PostgreSQL wire protocol].

## Technology Stack
* **Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL**: Provides relational storage, multi-AZ failover, and global replication.
* **Amazon RDS Proxy**: Prevents connection exhaustion and handles IAM token management.
* **AWS KMS**: Enforces encryption-at-rest using customer-managed keys (CMK).
* **PostgreSQL `pgaudit`**: Enables detailed audit logging for GDPR/CCPA compliance.
* **AWS CloudWatch & CloudTrail**: Monitors replica lag, connections, and system audit logs.

## Rationale
This architecture guarantees 99.95% uptime and high scalability for 1M MAU through connection pooling and automated read scaling. Regional active-local writes and encrypted global storage ensure strict GDPR and CCPA compliance.

Amazon DynamoDB.analysis:
## Overview
The Online Bookstore uses Amazon DynamoDB as a low-latency NoSQL datastore to manage high-throughput catalog, cart, and session operational data. It supports global active-active replication, strict data privacy compliance, and sub-10ms performance for 1M MAU.

## Key Elements
* Request Router / API Frontend
* Partition Router & Storage Nodes
* Storage Engine (B+-Tree & LSM-like indexing)
* Streams Processor (DynamoDB Streams)
* Global Tables (Multi-region active-active)

## Relationships
* Core E-Commerce Container -> Request Router: Reads/writes shopping cart & session state [HTTPS / DynamoDB API]
* Request Router -> Partition Router & Storage Nodes: Routes internal RPC requests [TCP / Consistent Hashing]
* Partition Router & Storage Nodes -> Storage Engine: Executes persistent B+-Tree updates [Local PCIe/SATA]
* Storage Engine -> Streams Processor: Triggers change data capture events [Internal Memory Buffers]
* Streams Processor -> Amazon SQS / SNS: Publishes item-level modification events [HTTPS / JSON]

## Technology Stack
* Amazon DynamoDB: Selected for predictable sub-10ms latency and high scalability.
* DynamoDB Streams: Used for asynchronous change data capture and event-driven integration.
* AWS KMS (CMK): Enforces encryption-at-rest with multi-region cryptographic isolation.
* DynamoDB Global Tables: Provides active-active multi-region replication across `us-east-1`, `eu-west-1`, and `ap-southeast-1`.
* Terraform / CloudFormation: Ensures infrastructure as code and automated drift detection.

## Rationale
This architecture ensures 99.95% uptime and low-latency performance to meet strict page-load requirements. It satisfies GDPR and CCPA mandates through localized KMS encryption, Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR), and strict PII data minimization.

Amazon ElastiCache Redis.analysis:
## Overview
The Online Bookstore is a scaled-down Amazon-style e-commerce platform designed to provide a fast, secure, and compliant shopping experience for physical and electronic books. It delivers resilient catalogue browsing, cart management, reviews, and recommendations supporting 1M monthly active users.

## Key Elements
* **Users & External Systems**: Guest/Registered Buyers, Store Administrators, Third-Party Vendors, Stripe/PayPal, FedEx/UPS, AWS SES, AWS Cognito/Auth0.
* **Frontend Container**: React.js Single Page Application hosted on AWS S3 and distributed via CloudFront.
* **API Gateway**: AWS API Gateway performing JWT validation via AWS Cognito and rate limiting.
* **Backend Containers**: Node.js/TypeScript Core E-Commerce, Python/FastAPI Recommendation & Review, and Node.js Tax & Currency containers deployed on Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate.
* **Databases & Caching**: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, Amazon DynamoDB, and Amazon ElastiCache Redis clusters (`cache-cart`, `cache-rec`, `cache-limit`).
* **Integration**: Amazon SQS / SNS Event Bus.

## Relationships
* **React.js SPA -> AWS API Gateway**: Routes client requests securely [HTTPS / REST & GraphQL].
* **AWS API Gateway -> Rate Limiter Component (`cache-limit`)**: Evaluates rate-limiting counters [RESP over TLS 1.3].
* **Core E-Commerce Container -> Cart Cache Component (`cache-cart`)**: Persists active shopping sessions and cart state [RESP over TLS 1.3].
* **Recommendation & Review Container -> Recommendation Cache Component (`cache-rec`)**: Reads and writes pre-computed product recommendations [RESP over TLS 1.3].
* **Core E-Commerce Container -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL**: Stores transactional order and catalogue data [PostgreSQL Wire Protocol over TLS].

## Technology Stack
* **Cloud Infrastructure**: AWS across `us-east-1`, `eu-west-1`, and `ap-southeast-1` for high availability and regional compliance.
* **Compute**: Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate for serverless container orchestration.
* **Caching & Storage**: Amazon ElastiCache Redis OSS with workload segregation (`noeviction` for carts, `allkeys-lru` for recommendations, `volatile-ttl` for rate limiting) and Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL.
* **Security & Auth**: AWS Cognito, Redis ACLs for least privilege, AWS KMS for encryption-in-transit (TLS 1.3) and at-rest.

## Rationale
This microservices-based architecture uses isolated Amazon ElastiCache Redis components to prevent noisy-neighbor memory exhaustion, protecting checkout resilience and maintaining sub-10ms cache latency. Multi-AZ AWS Fargate deployment and robust data partitioning guarantee 99.95% uptime and OWASP compliance under 1M MAU scale.

Event Bus & Integration.analysis:
## Overview
The Event Bus & Integration container provides asynchronous event routing, messaging, and data streaming for the Online Bookstore. It decouples microservices, securely integrates with third-party APIs, and maintains GDPR/CCPA compliance.

## Key Elements
- Event Router (`AWS EventBridge`)
- Notification Queue (`Amazon SQS`)
- Integration Dispatcher (`AWS Lambda`)
- Audit Streamer (`Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose`)
- Notification Status Tracker (`Amazon DynamoDB / AWS Lambda`)
- Dead Letter Queues (DLQs) and S3 Audit Store

## Relationships
- Core E-Commerce Container -> Event Router: Publishes domain events [JSON over AWS SNS/EventBridge]
- Event Router -> Notification Queue: Forwards background tasks [AWS SQS]
- Notification Queue -> Integration Dispatcher: Triggers asynchronous processing [AWS Lambda Event Source Mapping]
- Event Router -> Audit Streamer: Streams order lifecycle events [AWS EventBridge Target / Kinesis]
- Audit Streamer -> Secure Analytics Store (S3): Persists immutable audit logs [HTTPS / AWS S3 API]

## Technology Stack
- AWS EventBridge: Selected for content-based event routing across microservices.
- Amazon SQS & DLQs: Chosen for asynchronous backpressure handling and isolation of poisoned messages.
- AWS Lambda: Used for secure third-party webhook dispatching and PII tokenization.
- Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose: Deployed for high-throughput, scalable audit logging.
- AWS KMS: Enforces encryption-at-rest with customer-managed keys (CMKs) for all message buses and stores.

## Rationale
This architecture guarantees 99.95% uptime and reliable message processing through decoupled queuing and idempotent execution. It satisfies strict GDPR/CCPA compliance mandates via TLS 1.3 encryption, KMS key management, and edge PII masking.
